design_reasoning.rationale: Token format, revocation, replay, and clock-skew decisions compare alternatives and define reconsideration triggers.

observable_requirements.description: Compare stateful sessions and bounded signed tokens with explicit operational trade-offs.
Implement the selected verification and authorization boundary with explicit injected policies.

architecture_maintainability.rationale: Verification, authorization, replay control, rate policy, and audit output are isolated behind stable interfaces.

observable_requirements.description: Compose independently replaceable verification, replay, scope, and audit policies.
Demonstrate that a policy replacement does not bypass token verification invariants.

security_by_design.rationale: Threats including signature confusion, replay, scope escalation, timing leakage, and clock abuse map to controls.

observable_requirements.description: Define assets, trust boundaries, attacks, controls, and residual operational risk.
Reject algorithm confusion, malformed encoding, invalid time bounds, and signature mismatch.
Consume bounded token identifiers and reject reuse inside the configured replay window.

testing_evidence.rationale: Risk-based tests cover malformed encodings, timing boundaries, replay races, scope escalation, and policy isolation.

observable_requirements.description: Exercise malformed tokens, signature confusion, expiration, not-before, and scope escalation.
Exercise duplicate identifiers, window expiry, capacity bounds, and concurrent consumption semantics.

documentation_operations.rationale: Deployment-neutral integration, rotation, observable denial, incident containment, and recovery are documented.

observable_requirements.description: Document configuration, key identifiers, scope policy, and denial responses.
Document key rotation, replay-store failure, containment, rollback, and audit handling.

repository_hygiene.rationale: Pinned dependencies, license, CI policy, security disclosure, and contribution controls support maintenance.

observable_requirements.description: Commit deterministic dependency resolution for reproducible static review.
Publish a recognized license permitting use, modification, and redistribution.
Define lint, unit, and policy checks without asserting their execution outcome.
Provide private vulnerability reporting and supported-version boundaries.
Require tests and threat-model updates for security boundary changes.

implemented_safeguards.threat: An attacker supplies a malformed or algorithm-confused token to bypass verification.
implemented_safeguards.control: The verifier accepts one explicit algorithm and validates encoding, signature, issuer, audience, and time bounds.

implemented_safeguards.threat: A captured valid token is reused within its authorization lifetime.
implemented_safeguards.control: A bounded replay store atomically consumes token identifiers until their expiration boundary.

negative_boundary_cases.behavior: Reject tokens whose declared algorithm differs from the configured verifier.
Reject a valid token that lacks every scope required by the requested operation.
Allow only one successful consumption for the same token identifier.

track_evidence.rationale: The product primarily prevents authorization bypass, token replay, and privilege escalation at a concrete security boundary.

known_limitations.description: The in-memory replay adapter must be replaced by an atomic shared store for multi-process use.
Key generation and hardware-backed custody remain deployment responsibilities outside this library.

excluded_runtime_claims: Whether the project builds or starts
Performance, scaling, or reliability under load
Ability to extend the system safely
